description:
Tested with Darling built from the master branch (commit a5d378369, November 2026) plus the pending OpenGL context fix (darling#2145), on Debian 13 (kernel 6.12, x86_64 host), X11 (Xvfb with the xfwm4 window manager), 1920x1080. The application is a 32-bit (i386) build, version 4.0.0 (build 104.0.0).

Installation: the application was extracted into /Applications in the Darling prefix from the ZIP archive. It was started by running its binary directly.

Needed on the host: 32-bit applications require vm.mmap_min_addr to be 4096 or lower (sudo sysctl vm.mmap_min_addr=4096); the usual distribution default of 65536 prevents the binary from being mapped. This is a general setting for i386 applications, not a workaround for this game.

What works: the window opens and the game goes full screen, shows the title screen, the episode and level selection screens, and plays levels. Dragging the slingshot with the mouse and releasing launches a bird, physics, scoring and the camera movement work, and level 1-2 was cleared with the "Level cleared" screen and a saved score. Sound works: the game appears as a playback stream on PulseAudio, and a capture of the sink monitor during a level showed continuous music and effects (about 7.8 seconds, every 100 ms window audible). Cmd+Q quits the game cleanly and it can be started again afterwards. The log shows only two "unimplemented" warnings for touch-related view methods (setAcceptsTouchEvents: and setWantsRestingTouches:) at start-up; no crashes or hangs occurred.

What does not work: the start-up splash is drawn wrongly. After launch the window first shows blank white, then a static Rovio logo for about 8 seconds, drawn in only the upper-left part of the full-screen window with grey and black bars around it, then a loading picture and the title screen. The game itself is not affected. This version of the game ships no intro video (its bundle contains no video files), so there is no video to play.

Installation note: Darling's ditto currently fails to extract this ZIP archive, so it was unpacked with unzip in the Darling shell instead.
